security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI's sbi_dbtr_read_trig, sbi_dbtr_install_triggers, or sbi_dbtr_update_trig uses >= (greater-or-equal) instead of > (strictly greater) in the range check against trig_max (total_trigs), causing valid requests operating on the full trigger set (e.g., trig_count == trig_max or trig_idx_base + trig_count == trig_max, which references triggers 0 through trig_max-1 inclusive) to be incorrectly rejected with SBI_ERR_BAD_RANGE.
security_spec.summary: Off-by-one boundary check in SBI debug trigger range validation: using >= instead of > against trig_max rejects legitimate requests operating on all available triggers (0..trig_max-1), causing denial of debug functionality for S-mode software.

findings.finding: Post-fix, the range check correctly uses > (strictly greater) for trig_idx_base + trig_count > hs->total_trigs and returns SBI_ERR_BAD_RANGE. The trig_idx_base >= total_trigs check is correct because trigger indices are 0-based (idx == total_trigs is out of range). Reading trig_count == total_trigs - trig_idx_base (all remaining triggers) is now correctly allowed.

sbi_dbtr_install_trig lacks a trig_count > hs->total_trigs check returning SBI_ERR_BAD_RANGE as required by spec Table 100. Instead, it only checks hs->available_trigs < trig_count with return SBI_ERR_FAILED, which is a different error code and a different predicate (availability vs. validity). While functionally available_trigs <= total_trigs means trig_count > total_trigs would also fail the availability check, the spec-mandated error code SBI_ERR_BAD_RANGE is never returned, and the error is semantically wrong (resource exhaustion vs. invalid parameter).

Post-fix, the range check correctly uses > (strictly greater) for trig_count > hs->total_trigs and returns SBI_ERR_BAD_RANGE. Updating trig_count == total_trigs (all triggers) is now correctly allowed.
